Predict at new covariate values

Source: R/methods_generic.R
predict.tulpa_fit.Rd

Prediction of the linear predictor at newdata, on the link or response scale. The fixed-effect part is X beta with credible bounds from the fixed-effect covariance (vcov()).

Formula random effects are conditioned on, as lme4 does: a row of a group the fit saw takes the posterior mean of that group's effect, and a row of a group it did not see takes the prior mean, zero, with an interval that carries the between-group spread – its effect is drawn from the term's covariance, at each posterior draw of it where the fit samples or integrates the covariance and at its estimate or conditioned value otherwise. re_form = NA gives the population prediction (every random effect at zero); a one-sided formula such as ~ (1 | site) conditions on that term alone. With random effects the interval is read over 4000 pinned draws of the fixed and random effects jointly (the same on every call), and se.fit is the SD of those draws.

A fit carrying a latent field adds it to the prediction by default (include_field = TRUE), on every backend and at the training design as at newdata. The fit's latent posterior is a mixture of Gaussians in the coefficients and the fields at their fitted support (the mesh nodes, the fitted locations, the basis coefficients, the areal units, the fitted times): one per hyperparameter cell on a nested-Laplace grid, the one cell of a fit at fixed hyperparameters (mode = "laplace"), and one point per stored draw on a sampler fit (mode = "hmc" and its siblings, "gibbs"). The field at a row is its conditional distribution given that fitted field: the mesh projector there for an SPDE field (spatial_spde()), the basis re-evaluated there (on the domain the fit was built on) for an HSGP field (spatial_gp(approx = "hsgp")), the NNGP predictive given the field at the nearest fitted locations for a GP / NNGP field (spatial_gp()), the sum of its scales for spatial_multiscale(), and the value of the row's own unit or time for an areal (ICAR / CAR / BYM2) or temporal (RW1 / RW2 / AR1) field. newdata then carries the field's unit column (the one named in spatial(...)), time column and group column; a unit the fit was not fitted at is refused, since the field carries no value there. A temporal walk or GP (temporal_rw1(), temporal_rw2(), temporal_ar1(), temporal_gp()) at a time it was not fitted at is drawn from its conditional given the fitted path: the recursion run past the fitted times (whole steps of their equal spacing), the Brownian bridge between them for RW1, the GP conditional at any time; RW2 / AR1 between fitted times or off the step lattice are refused. An s() smoother is read at the node the fit binned the row's covariate value into (a value outside the fitted range is refused), a spatiotemporal() interaction at the row's area and time, an inline field replicated by a factor (spatial(..., by =)) in the copy of the row's level, and a latent() block at the training rows only. A fit carrying a latent term the prediction cannot be read for is refused, naming the term, rather than predicted without it. A restricted field (spatial_rsr()) is the field less its projection on the restriction design fitted at the support, w - x' (X_u' X_u)^-1 X_u' w, with x the design of the fitted unit or location a row sits at and otherwise the restriction formula evaluated on newdata. fit is the exact posterior mean of the linear predictor, and se.fit / lower / upper are read over 4000 pinned draws of the cell, the coefficients, the field and its conditional at the rows, so the interval carries the uncertainty of the coefficients and the field, an NNGP field's conditional (kriging) variance away from the data, and the spread of the hyperparameters. These are the draws posterior_linpred() and posterior_predict() return at the same newdata.

A spatially or temporally varying coefficient (spatial_svc(), temporal_tvc()) is predicted at the newdata coordinates / times from every posterior draw: an NNGP field by the NNGP predictive at the nearest fitted locations, an HSGP field by its basis evaluated there (inside the basis domain only); a "gp" time path by the GP conditional at any time, an "rw1" path by a Brownian bridge between fitted levels and Brownian steps past them, "rw2" and "ar1" paths by their recursion at whole grid steps past the fitted levels. Uncertainty grows with distance from the data and with the forecast horizon, and the bounds are pointwise. A time between the levels of an "rw2" / "ar1" fit, a time off its step lattice, a time beyond unequally spaced levels on any grid structure, a factor level the fit did not see, and a group without a fitted path are refused with the reason. fit is then the posterior mean of the linear predictor and se.fit / lower / upper are its posterior SD and quantiles.

A tulpa_nested_laplace_joint() fit (no model formula) is predicted for one response arm at newdata, a list: X is the arm's design at the new rows, with the columns of the arm's fitted X in their order, and each latent term reaching the arm is placed by the entry it needs – index, each row's unit (areal unit, time, group, location) per block, a list of integer vectors by block position, by b<k> or by the block's name; coords, the rows' coordinates, for an hsgp block given by its coordinates (a basis builder: coords, m, c), whose basis is rebuilt there on the fitted domain; basis for an hsgp block given by its basis; weight for a block's per-row design weight (svc_weight, or one per field for field_weight); projector for a projected block; re_idx, each row's group for the arm's random intercepts (NA for a group the fit did not see, whose effect is drawn from its sigma_re); and offset. Each block enters at its amplitude on the arm – a copy arm's alpha times the field SD, a field_coef, an iid block's SD – as the fit's own linear predictor takes it. Within each outer-grid cell the linear predictor is Gaussian, with the cell's mode and covariance (read off the cell's precision, which the fit keeps by default when it carries a latent term, control$store_Q); the prediction is the weighted mixture of those Gaussians over the cells, so lower / upper are the mixture's quantiles. A fit with store_Q = FALSE reports the uncertainty only for rows that load on the fixed effects and basis-builder blocks alone.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tulpa_fit'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  type = c("link", "response"),
  se.fit = FALSE,
  level = 0.95,
  include_field = TRUE,
  re_form = NULL,
  arm = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A tulpa_fit object.

newdata

Data frame of covariates (and, for a field fit, the field's coordinate columns, unit column or time and group columns; for a varying-coefficient fit, its coordinate / time and group columns). If NULL, predicts at the training design (requires $model_matrix).

type

"link" (linear predictor) or "response" (mean scale, E[y]). For a binomial fit the "response" scale here is the per-trial success probability g^{-1}(eta) (there is no n_trials at newdata); this differs from fitted(), which returns the trial-scaled expected count at the training design. On a zero-inflated fit (ziformula) the "link" scale is the count predictor and the "response" scale is the mixture mean (1 - pi) E[y | eta], pi = plogis(X_zi beta_zi), with the zero-inflation design rebuilt from the fit's ziformula at newdata.

se.fit

If TRUE, also return the link-scale standard error and credible bounds. On a zero-inflated fit se.fit is the count predictor's, and the response-scale bounds are quantiles of the mixture mean over draws of the count and zero-inflation coefficients jointly (pinned, so repeated calls agree).

level

Credible-interval level (default 0.95).

include_field

For a fit with a latent field (continuous, areal or temporal), add the field to the prediction (default TRUE), and for a varying-coefficient fit the coefficient field at the newdata coordinates / times. FALSE gives the prediction without them. Ignored for fits with no field.

re_form

Which formula random-effect terms to condition on, as lme4's re.form: NULL (default) every term, NA or ~0 none (the population level), or a one-sided formula naming a subset, e.g. ~ (1 | site). newdata then carries the grouping columns of the terms kept.

arm

For a tulpa_nested_laplace_joint() fit, the response arm to predict (its name or index); may be left NULL on a one-arm fit.

...

Ignored.

Value

If se.fit = FALSE, a numeric vector. If se.fit = TRUE, a data frame with fit, se.fit (link scale), lower, upper on the requested scale.
